dependent on one aggregate leading to accumulation, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise.

A state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution arises dependent on a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution.

dependent on the physical basis, the aggregates arise; one great primary … external … nutriment-produced … [and so on].
… mind-produced … one great primary of non-percipient beings … [and so on] … By way of not-object condition:

Condition: Aggregates leading to accumulation (*ācayagāmi*) are related to knowledge of the minds of others (*cetopariyañāṇa*), knowledge of recollection of past lives (*pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇa*), knowledge of the passing away and rebirth according to karma (*yathākammūpagañāṇa*), knowledge of future states (*anāgataṁsañāṇa*), and advertence (*āvajjanā*) by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*).
A state leading to diminution (*apacayagāmi*) is related to a state leading to accumulation by way of object-condition—the paths of the trainee (*sekkhā magga*).
Having emerged [from jhāna], they review the path; through the knowledge of penetration of minds, they know the mind of one possessing a mind leading to diminution.

The aggregates leading to diminution are a condition by way of object-condition for the knowledge of penetration of minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, and the knowledge of future existences.
A state leading to diminution is related to a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution by way of object condition:
an Arahant, having emerged from the path, reviews the path; he knows with the knowledge of penetration of minds (cetopariyañāṇa) the mind of one possessing a mind leading to diminution;
aggregates leading to diminution are related to the knowledge of penetration of minds and the knowledge of recollection of past lives.
Knowledge of the future is related to adverting by way of object condition.
A state that leads neither to accumulation nor to dispersal is related to a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to dispersal by way of object condition:
an Arahant reviews the fruit; he reviews Nibbāna; Nibbāna is related to the adverting of the fruit.
It is a condition by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*). An Arahant contemplates the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
[he contemplates] the ear ... pe ... the physical basis (*vatthu*) ... he contemplates the aggregates that lead neither to accumulation nor to dispersal as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;

he sees forms with the divine eye (*dibbacakkhu*); he hears sounds with the divine ear-element (*dibbā sotadhātu*); [he knows minds] with the knowledge of penetration of others' minds (*cetopariyañāṇa*).
One who possesses a consciousness that neither leads to accumulation nor leads to diminution knows the consciousness [of another].

The functional state of the base of infinite space is a condition, by way of object-condition, for the functional state of the base of infinite consciousness. The functional state of the base of nothingness [is a condition] for the functional state of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception ...

pe ... the visible-object-base is [a condition] for eye-consciousness ... pe ... the tangible-object-base is [a condition] for body-consciousness ... pe ... [the state] that neither leads to accumulation nor leads to diminution.

The aggregates are related to the knowledge of the modes of supernormal power, the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, and the knowledge of future existences,
as well as to adverting, by way of object condition.
A state that neither leads to accumulation nor leads to dispersal is related to a state that leads to accumulation by way of object condition— the trainee (sekha) states...
They review the fruit; they review Nibbāna. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage (gotrabhū) and purification (vodāna) by way of object-condition (ārammaṇa-paccaya).
Or, whether they be trainees (sekkhā) or worldlings (puthujjana), they practice insight into the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
they relish it and delight in it; with that as an object, lust arises ... pe ... grief arises. [The same applies to] the ear ... pe ... the physical base (vatthu).
... when they contemplate with insight the aggregates that lead neither to accumulation nor to diminution as impermanent, suffering, and non-self, they experience gratification and delight in them;
taking that as an object, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt ... pe ... restlessness ...
pe ... grief arises ... pe ... they see forms with the divine eye, and hear sounds with the divine ear-element.
They hear; by means of the knowledge of penetration of minds, they know the mind of one possessing a consciousness that leads neither to accumulation nor to dispersal.

The aggregates leading neither to accumulation nor to dispersal are related to the knowledge of the modes of psychic power, the knowledge of penetration of minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, and the knowledge of future existences by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*).

A state leading to accumulation and not leading to diminution is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state leading to diminution: Nibbāna is a condition, by way of object-condition, for the Path.
Predominance:
A state leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a state leading to accumulation: [as] object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*).
Co-nascent predominance. Object-predominance: having given a gift, undertaken virtue, or performed an observance-day duty, one esteems and reviews it;
one esteems and reviews former well-performed deeds; having emerged from jhāna, one esteems and reviews the jhāna;
one esteems, relishes, and delights in the aggregates leading to accumulation.
Taking that as an object, lust arises and wrong view arises. Conascence-predominance:
a predominance leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for its associated aggregates.

A state leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a state that is neither leading to accumulation nor leading to dispersal. Conascence-predominance: a predominance leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for mind-produced matter.
A state leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a state leading to accumulation, and for a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution.
As co-nascent predominance: a predominance leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.

A state leading to diminution is a condition for a state leading to diminution by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). Conascence-predominance: a predominance leading to diminution is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of predominance condition.

A state leading to diminution is a condition for a state leading to accumulation by way of predominance condition. Object-predominance: those in training (*sekkha*), having emerged from the path, esteem and review the path.
A state leading to decline is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to decline:
as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: an Arahant, having emerged from the Path, esteems and reviews the Path.
Conascence-predominance: a predominance leading to decline is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for mind-produced matter.
A state leading to diminution is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a state leading to diminution and for a state that neither leads to accumulation nor to diminution.
As co-nascent predominance: a predominance leading to diminution is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
A state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution is a condition, by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*), for a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution:
as object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*) and as co-nascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*). As object-predominance:
an Arahant, esteeming it, reviews the fruit; esteeming it, he reviews Nibbāna; Nibbāna is a predominance-condition for the fruit.

Condition. Conascence-predominance: A predominance that is neither leading to accumulation nor leading to dispersal is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
A state that is neither leading to accumulation nor leading to dispersal is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a state that leads to accumulation.
Object-predominance: Learners, esteeming the fruit, review it; esteeming Nibbāna, they review it.
Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage and purification by way of the predominance-condition.
Esteeming the eye, one relishes it … [as above] … esteeming the physical basis … esteeming the aggregates that lead neither to accumulation nor to dispersal, one relishes them and delights in them.
Taking that as an object, lust arises and wrong view arises.

A state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a state that leads to diminution. Object-predominance: Nibbāna is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for the Path. Proximity... [etc.]...
immediate succession.
A state leading to accumulation is a condition for a state leading to accumulation by way of proximity-condition:
preceding aggregates leading to accumulation are a condition for subsequent aggregates leading to accumulation by way of proximity-condition;
adaptation is a condition for change-of-lineage by way of proximity-condition; adaptation is a condition for purification by way of proximity-condition.

A state leading to accumulation is related to a state leading to diminution by way of proximity condition: change-of-lineage is related to the path by way of proximity condition; purification is related to the path by way of proximity condition.
A state leading to accumulation is related to a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution by way of proximity condition:
aggregates leading to accumulation are related to emergence by way of proximity condition; for those in training, conformity is related to the attainment of fruition by way of proximity condition.
For one emerging from cessation, wholesome consciousness of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is related to the attainment of the fruit by way of proximity condition.
A state leading to diminution is related to a state leading neither to accumulation nor to diminution by way of proximity condition—the path is related to the fruit by way of proximity condition.
A state leading neither to accumulation nor to diminution is related to a state leading neither to accumulation nor to diminution by way of proximity condition.

Condition: Preceding aggregates that neither lead to accumulation nor lead to diminution are a condition for subsequent aggregates that neither lead to accumulation nor lead to diminution by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
The life-continuum (*bhavaṅga*) is a condition for adverting; functional [consciousness] is a condition for emergence;

for an Arahant, conformity is a condition for the attainment of fruition; and for one emerging from cessation, the functional consciousness of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition.
The attainment of fruition is related to [the attainment of fruition] by way of proximity condition (*anantara-paccaya*).

A state that neither leads to accumulation nor leads to diminution is related to a state that leads to accumulation by way of proximity condition: adverting is related to the aggregates leading to accumulation by way of proximity condition.
[This applies to] the immediately preceding and so forth.
A state leading to accumulation is a condition for a state leading to accumulation by way of the immediately preceding condition ... pe ... (The same as the "immediately preceding" [condition]).
(In the section on dependence under the "conascent" condition, there are nine questions similar to the "conascent" section.

In the section on dependence under the "mutuality" condition, there are three similar to the "mutuality" [section]. In the section on conditions under the "support" condition, it is similar to the "support" section. For all four [conditions]—)
There is no separate occurrence. (Thirteen questions.
Strong-dependence:
A state leading to accumulation is related to a state leading to accumulation by way of strong-dependence condition—namely, object-strong-dependence (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*).
Proximity-strong-dependence, natural strong-dependence … [as appropriate] … Natural strong-dependence:

depending on faith leading to accumulation, one gives a gift, undertakes virtue … [and so on] … the observance-day rite … [and so on] … develops jhāna … [and so on] … insight … [and so on] … direct knowledge … [and so on] … attains meditative attainment;
one arouses conceit, adopts wrong view. [Depending on] virtue leading to accumulation … learning … generosity … [and so on].
… wisdom … lust … hatred … delusion … conceit … wrong view … aspiration. Depending on [these], one gives a gift;
observes virtue; … performs the Uposatha duties; … develops jhāna; … develops insight; … develops direct knowledge;
… develops attainment; kills a living being; … causes a schism in the Saṅgha. Faith leading to accumulation … wisdom, lust … aspiration.
Faith leading to accumulation ... pe ... wisdom is related to lust ... pe ... aspiration by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
The preparation for the first jhāna is related to the first jhāna by way of decisive support condition ...
The preparation for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is related to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception by way of decisive support condition.

Condition: The first jhāna is a condition for the second jhāna... [and so on] ...the base of nothingness is a condition for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
A state leading to accumulation is a condition for a state leading to dispersal by way of decisive support condition—namely, as immediate decisive support (*anantarūpanissaya*).

Natural strong-dependence condition … [as above] … Natural strong-dependence: the preparation for the first path is a condition for the first path by way of strong-dependence condition … [and so on] … the preparation for the fourth path is a condition for the fourth path by way of strong-dependence condition.
A state leading to accumulation is a condition for a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to dispersal by way of strong-dependence condition: as immediate strong-dependence … [and so on].
Natural decisive support … [as above] … Natural decisive support: depending on faith that leads to accumulation, one torments oneself, torments others, and experiences suffering rooted in striving.
[Depending on] virtue that leads to accumulation … [as above] … wisdom.
Depending on lust … [as above] … longing, one torments oneself, torments others, and experiences suffering rooted in striving.
One experiences [them]. Faith leading to accumulation … pe … wisdom.

Lust … pe … aspiration is a condition for bodily pleasure, bodily pain, and the attainment of fruition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*). Wholesome and unwholesome kamma is a condition for its result by way of decisive support condition.
A state leading to diminution is a condition for a state leading to diminution by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*). As natural decisive support:
the first path is a condition for the second path ... pe ... the third path is a condition for the fourth path by way of decisive support condition.
A state leading to diminution is a condition for a state leading to accumulation by way of decisive support condition: namely, object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*).

Natural strong-dependence … [as before] … Natural strong-dependence: Learners (sekkhā), depending on the path as a natural strong-dependence, produce unarisen wholesome attainments, enter attained ones, and practice insight into formations as impermanent, suffering, and non-self.

The path is a natural strong-dependence for the learners’ analytical knowledge of meaning (atthapaṭisambhidā) … [and so on] … for the analytical knowledge of expression (dhammapaṭisambhidā), for the analytical knowledge of philology (niruttipaṭisambhidā), and for skill in [discerning] the possible and the impossible (ṭhānāṭhānakosalla).
It is a condition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state leading to diminution (*apacayagāmi*) is a condition for a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution (*nevācayagāmināpacayagāmi*) by way of decisive support condition—namely, object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, natural decisive support … [and so on] … Natural decisive support: an Arahant, having relied upon the Path (*magga*) as a decisive support…

One produces an unarisen functional attainment (*kiriyasamāpatti*), enters an arisen one... [and so on] ...skill in discerning what is possible and impossible is a condition for [the arising of such skill] by way of decisive support condition (*upanissayapaccaya*).
The path is a condition for the attainment of fruition (*phalasamāpatti*) by way of decisive support condition.
A state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution is a condition for a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution by way of decisive support condition.
Condition: object-strong-dependence, proximity-strong-dependence, natural strong-dependence … [and so on] … Natural strong-dependence:
depending on bodily pleasure, one torments oneself, torments oneself thoroughly, and experiences suffering rooted in searching.
Depending on bodily pain … weather … food … lodging, one torments oneself, torments oneself thoroughly.

… pe … bodily pleasure … bodily pain … temperature … food … and lodging are related to bodily pleasure, bodily pain, and the attainment of fruition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

An Arahant, relying on bodily pleasure as a decisive support, arouses an unarisen functional attainment (*kiriyasamāpatti*) … pe … and practices insight (*vipassati*). Bodily pain … [is likewise related].
[One] contemplates temperature … nutriment … the resting place by way of decisive support … [and so on] … one sees with insight.
A state leading neither to accumulation nor to dispersal is a condition, by way of decisive support condition, for a state leading to accumulation:
as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, natural decisive support … [and so on] … Natural decisive support: having relied upon bodily pleasure … [and so on].
One gives a gift … [as above] … one arouses meditative attainment; one kills a living being … [as above] … one causes a schism in the Saṅgha.
By depending on bodily pain, climate, food, or lodging, one gives a gift … [as above] … one causes a schism in the Saṅgha.
By depending on bodily pleasure … [as above] … lodging, one [depends] on faith leading to accumulation … [as above] … wisdom, lust … [as above] … aspiration.
It is a condition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state that leads neither to accumulation nor to dispersal is a condition for a state that leads to dispersal by way of decisive support condition—namely, as an object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*) or as a natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … [as before] … Natural decisive support: relying on bodily pleasure, one generates the Path.

Bodily suffering …pe… by depending on a lodging one generates the path; bodily pleasure, bodily suffering …pe… the lodging is a condition for the path by way of the decisive-support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
Prenascence (*purejāta*).
A state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution is a condition, by way of pre-arising condition, for a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution:
namely, object-pre-arising and base-pre-arising. Regarding object-pre-arising: an Arahant contemplates the eye ... [and so on] ...
the base as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; he sees forms with the divine eye; with the divine ear ... [and so on].
One hears a sound with the ear-element; the visible-base is a condition for eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the tangible-base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of prenascence-condition.

As base-prenascence: the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness … [and so on] … the physical basis (vatthu) is a condition for aggregates that neither lead to accumulation nor lead to dispersal by way of prenascence-condition.
A state leading to accumulation or leading to diminution is a condition, by way of prenascence condition, for a state leading to accumulation—namely, object-prenascence and base-prenascence.

Regarding object-prenascence: when trainees or worldlings practice insight into the eye … [and so on] … into the base as impermanent, suffering, and non-self, they relish it and delight in it; taking that as their object, lust arises.
...pe... sorrow arises; one sees a form with the divine eye, hears a sound with the divine ear-element. Base-prenascence:
the base is a condition, by way of prenascence-condition, for the aggregates leading to accumulation.

A state that leads neither to accumulation nor to dispersal is a condition, by way of prenascence-condition, for a state leading to dispersal. Base-prenascence: the base is a condition, by way of prenascence-condition, for the aggregates leading to dispersal.

A posteriorly-arisen state leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of posteriority-condition, for a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to dispersal: the posteriorly-arisen aggregates leading to accumulation are a condition, by way of posteriority-condition, for this pre-arisen body.

A posteriorly-arisen state leading to dispersal is a condition, by way of posteriority-condition, for a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to dispersal: the posteriorly-arisen aggregates leading to dispersal are a condition, by way of posteriority-condition, for this pre-arisen body.
A state that neither leads to accumulation nor leads to diminution is a condition, by way of postnascence condition, for a state that neither leads to accumulation nor leads to diminution:
postnascent aggregates that neither lead to accumulation nor lead to diminution are a condition, by way of postnascence condition, for this prenascent body.
(Repetition)
A state leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of repetition-condition, for a state leading to accumulation:
preceding aggregates leading to accumulation are a condition, by way of repetition-condition, for succeeding aggregates leading to accumulation;
adaptation is a condition, by way of repetition-condition, for change-of-lineage; adaptation is a condition, by way of repetition-condition, for purification.

A state leading to accumulation is related to a state leading to non-accumulation by way of the condition of repetition: change-of-lineage to the path; purification is related to the path by way of the condition of repetition.
A state leading neither to accumulation nor to non-accumulation is related to a state leading neither to accumulation nor to non-accumulation by way of the condition of repetition:
preceding aggregates leading neither to accumulation nor to non-accumulation are related to succeeding aggregates leading neither to accumulation nor to non-accumulation...
The aggregates are related to the aggregates by way of the condition of repetition.
Kamma:

A state leading to accumulation is related to a state leading to accumulation by way of the condition of kamma. Volition leading to accumulation is related to the associated aggregates by way of the condition of kamma.
A state leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution—both conascent and asynchronous.
Conascent: volition leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for mind-produced matter. Asynchronous:
volition leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates and for kamma-born matter.
A state leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state leading to accumulation and for a state that neither leads to accumulation nor leads to diminution:
volition leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.

A state leading to diminution is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state leading to diminution: volition leading to diminution is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the associated aggregates.
A state leading to diminution is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state that is neither leading to accumulation nor leading to diminution:
[this is] both conascent and asynchronous. Conascent: volition leading to diminution is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for mind-produced matter.
Condition. As asynchronous: volition leading to diminution is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates.
A state leading to diminution is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state leading to diminution and for a state that neither leads to accumulation nor to diminution:
volition leading to diminution is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
Conditioned by way of kamma-condition:
A state that leads neither to accumulation nor to dispersal is related to a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to dispersal by way of kamma-condition—
namely, volition leading neither to accumulation nor to dispersal is related to its associated aggregates and to mind-produced matter.

Material phenomena are related to material phenomena by way of kamma-condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, volition that leads neither to accumulation nor to disintegration is related to its associated aggregates and to the material phenomena of the kamma-born (kaṭattā-rūpa) by way of kamma-condition.
Resultant...
A state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution is a condition, by way of resultant condition (*vipākapaccaya*), for a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution:

one resultant aggregate leading neither to accumulation nor to diminution is a condition for three aggregates … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … the aggregates are a condition for the physical basis by way of resultant condition.

A state leading to accumulation, such as nutriment and so forth, is a condition for a state leading to accumulation by way of the condition of nutriment … by way of the condition of faculty … by way of the condition of jhāna … by way of the condition of path … by way of the condition of association.
Dissociation … [condition].
A state leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to dispersal:
namely, conascence and postnascence. As conascence: conascent aggregates leading to accumulation are a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for mind-produced matter.
As postnascence: postnascent aggregates leading to accumulation are a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for this prenascent body.
A state leading to diminution is a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution:
namely, conascence and postnascence. As conascence: conascent aggregates leading to diminution are a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for mind-produced matter.
As postnascence: postnascent aggregates leading to diminution are a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for this prenascent body.
A state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution is a condition, by way of dissociation-condition (*vippayutta-paccaya*), for a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to diminution:
namely, conascence (*sahajāta*), prenascence (*purejāta*), and postnascence (*pacchājāta*). As conascence:

aggregates that lead neither to accumulation nor to diminution are a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for mind-produced matter. At the moment of rebirth-linking, [aggregates] that lead neither to accumulation nor to diminution...
The aggregates are related to derived matter by way of dissociation condition. The aggregates are related to the physical basis by way of dissociation condition.
The physical basis is related to the aggregates by way of dissociation condition. As pre-arisen:
the eye-base to eye-consciousness … pe … the body-base to body-consciousness … pe … the physical basis to the aggregates that lead neither to accumulation nor to dispersal.
It is a condition by way of dissociation-condition (*vippayutta-paccaya*). Postnascent aggregates that lead neither to accumulation nor to dispersal are related to this prenascent body... [etc.

...A state leading neither to accumulation nor to dispersal is a condition for a state leading to accumulation by way of dissociation-condition. Prenascent: the physical basis (*vatthu*) is a condition for the aggregates leading to accumulation by way of dissociation-condition.

A state leading to non-accumulation and leading to diminution is a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for a state leading to diminution. As pre-nascence: the (heart-)base is a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for the aggregates leading to diminution.
Existence, etc.:

A state leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for a state leading to accumulation—one aggregate leading to accumulation is a condition for three aggregates … pe … [and so on].
A state leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to dispersal:
namely, co-nascence and post-nascence. As co-nascence: the co-nascent aggregates leading to accumulation are a condition, by way of presence-condition, for mind-produced matter. As post-nascence:
the post-nascent aggregates leading to accumulation are a condition, by way of presence-condition, for this pre-nascent body.
A state leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for a state leading to accumulation and for a state leading neither to accumulation nor to diminution:
one aggregate leading to accumulation is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter … two aggregates … [and so on] … pe … .
A state leading to decline... three [factors]. (To be done according to the method for states leading to accumulation.
A state leading neither to accumulation nor to decline is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for a state leading neither to accumulation nor to decline:
conascence, prenascence, postnascence, nutriment, and faculty. Conascent: a state leading neither to accumulation nor to decline...

One aggregate is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter … two aggregates … [and so on] … At the moment of rebirth-linking … aggregates are a condition, by way of presence-condition, for the physical basis;
the physical basis is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for the aggregates. One great primary … external … nutriment-produced … [and so on].
… kamma-originated … non-percipient beings … [and so on] … Pre-arisen: an Arahant, with regard to the eye … [and so on] … contemplates the basis as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
he sees a visible form with the divine eye; he hears a sound with the divine ear-element;
the visible-form base [is related] to eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the tangible-object base [is related] to body-consciousness.

…pe… the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness …pe… the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness …pe… the physical basis (vatthu) is a condition by way of presence-condition for the aggregates that lead neither to accumulation nor to dispersal.
Post-nascent aggregates that lead neither to accumulation nor to dispersal are a condition by way of presence-condition for this pre-nascent body.
Edible food is a condition for this body …pe…. The material life-faculty is a condition for the types of matter produced by kamma …pe….
A state leading to accumulation or leading to diminution is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for a state leading to accumulation. As pre-arisen:
whether they be trainees (sekkhā) or worldlings (puthujjana), they practice insight into the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; they relish it and delight in it.

Taking that as object, lust arises … [and so on] … or grief arises. [They likewise do so with] the ear … [and so on] … they practice insight into the physical basis (vatthu) as impermanent … [and so on] … [lust or grief arises].
They relish it and delight in it; with that as their object, lust... [down to] ...grief arises.
One sees a form with the divine eye, hears a sound with the divine ear-element; the physical basis is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for the aggregates leading to accumulation.

A state leading to accumulation and a state leading neither to accumulation nor to diminution are related to a state leading to diminution by way of presence condition. Pre-nascence: The (heart-)base is related to the aggregates leading to diminution by way of presence condition.

States leading to accumulation and states leading neither to accumulation nor to diminution are related to a state leading to accumulation by way of presence condition—by way of conascence and pre-nascence.
Conascent: One aggregate leading to accumulation and the (heart-)base are related to three [other aggregates]...
